assertions.text: Policy thresholds (650/600 credit scores) appear in a dedicated policy column (e.g. 'Credit threshold') separate from the applicant's actual credit score column. The reader sees both the threshold and the score, making the comparison explicit. Not just threshold values used as data in the score column.
assertions.evidence: Tables have only 'Credit Score' column with actual scores (651, 650, 750). No separate 'Credit threshold' column exists. Thresholds appear only in scenario names and @Description text.

assertions.text: Cell values use concrete domain terms (e.g. '70', '650', 'APPROVED') — not abstract codes like 'CATEGORY_A' or '1'. Boolean true/false is acceptable for yes/no flags when the parameter type is boolean.
assertions.evidence: Table values: 651, 650, 750, true, false, APPROVED, REJECTED, PENDING_REVIEW. All concrete domain terms.

assertions.text: Table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column
assertions.evidence: First column in all three tables: '| Scenario | Credit Score |', '| Scenario | Customer Age |'

assertions.text: Scenario names describe conditions ('Senior at lower threshold', 'Missing income') — not outcomes ('Approved', 'Rejected').
assertions.evidence: Names describe conditions: 'Just above threshold with income', 'Senior without income', 'Age boundary: non-senior at age 64'

assertions.text: Column names use domain/business language (e.g. 'Age', 'Credit score', 'Stable income', 'Decision?') — not code identifiers like 'customerAge', 'boolean'.
assertions.evidence: Column names: 'Scenario', 'Credit Score', 'Stable Income', 'Result?', 'Customer Age' — all business language

assertions.text: At least one output column name ends with '?' (e.g. 'Decision?' or 'Status?')
assertions.evidence: All three tables have '| Result?' column

assertions.text: Test method body contains no if or switch statements
assertions.evidence: All method bodies contain only: assertEquals(result, loanService.evaluateLoan(...))

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
Test method has either a @DisplayName annotation or a method name that reads as a clear, descriptive title when converted from camelCase/snake_case.
assertions.evidence: @DisplayName("Standard applicant credit threshold"), @DisplayName("Senior applicant lower threshold...")

assertions.text: If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string """), not string concatenation with +. Passes if @Description is absent.
assertions.evidence: @Description("""...""")": all three methods use triple-quote text blocks

assertions.text: Multiple tables (or @TableTest methods) are used, each addressing a distinct concern — not one monolithic table mixing unrelated rules. Acceptable to use a single table only when the domain genuinely has a single concern.
assertions.evidence: Three distinct methods: standardApplicantCreditThreshold, seniorApplicantLowerThreshold, missingIncomeTriggersReview

assertions.text: Each table has only the rows needed to express its concern's rules — no unnecessary permutations from combining concerns. Fewer rows per table is expected when concerns are properly separated.
assertions.evidence: Method 1: 5 rows for credit boundary; Method 2: 8 rows for senior+age boundary; Method 3: 5 rows for null income. Each focused.

assertions.text: Age boundary policy, credit score categorisation, and income status are separated into distinct @TableTest methods, with a method combining these for the expected verdict
assertions.evidence: Three methods test age boundary, credit score, and income separately, but there is no fourth method combining all three into an overall verdict.

assertions.text: Scenario descriptions and @Description text do not include specific field values that are already visible in the table or that serve as 'any valid value' placeholders. Stating 'Customer age is 35 for all rows' in @Description when age is fixed in the method body, or including fixed values in scenario names that are already columns, adds maintenance burden without value. Describe the scenario condition or policy being tested instead.
assertions.evidence: @Description: 'Customer age is 35 for all rows (non-senior)' — this is the exact example given in the assertion as redundant when age is already fixed in method body.

assertions.text: The standardApplicantCreditThreshold table (or equivalent non-senior table) clearly documents the effect of stable income: rows show that above-threshold credit score + stable income = APPROVED, and above-threshold credit score + no stable income = REJECTED. The stable income parameter's effect on the outcome must be visible from the table rows, not just implied.
assertions.evidence: Table rows show: 'Well above with income | 750 | true | APPROVED' and 'Above threshold, no income | 751 | false | REJECTED' — effect is explicit.
